question: A 72-year-old patient with known COPD has an SpO2 of 86% on room air and a PaCO2 of 58 mmHg on recent ABG. Which oxygen delivery device is most appropriate to initiate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A non-rebreather mask delivers FiO2 0.8–1.0, far exceeding the safe target for a hypercapnic COPD patient and risking CO2 narcosis.
Nasal cannula at 6 L/min delivers approximately FiO2 0.44, which is unpredictable and potentially too high for this patient with chronic hypercapnia.

answers.text: 28% Venturi mask at the manufacturer-specified flow rate

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A 28% Venturi mask delivers a precise, controlled FiO2 targeting SpO2 88–92% — the recommended range in hypercapnic COPD. This minimises the risk of worsening CO2 retention.
A simple face mask is a variable-performance device that delivers FiO2 0.35–0.60, which is uncontrolled and inappropriate for a patient requiring precise FiO2 titration.

overallFeedback.feedback: In hypercapnic COPD, you need precise FiO2 control. Only a fixed-performance device (Venturi mask) can guarantee this. Review the clinical applications section.
Excellent. The Venturi mask is the device of choice when precise, controlled FiO2 delivery is essential — particularly in hypercapnic COPD.
